# Request Parameters (dsh-request-params)
English | 中文
**Add your own parameters to every model request dsh sends.** OpenRouter provider routing, fallback
models, reasoning effort, sampling extras, gateway headers, or any JSON field a gateway accepts. Pic
k one of the channels dsh already has, add parameters on a page instead of in code, see exactly what
each request will carry before anything is sent, and see what the gateway answered afterwards.
## Why
dsh sends the fields its model adapters know about. Gateways such as OpenRouter take more: which pro
viders to use and in what order, fallback models, a reasoning budget, a session ID for cache affinit
y. dsh does not send OpenRouter's `provider` routing preferences. Plugins exist for single slices of
this (provider order and quantization, for example); this one is general. The same page handles any
field or header for any gateway, with a ready form for OpenRouter's routing options, a live preview
ader for any gateway, with a ready form for OpenRouter's routing options, a live preview, and a log.
Each *parameter* belongs to a channel (or names its own hosts, models, and paths) and says what to a
dd, replace, or remove in the body and headers. Parameters are applied to the request just before it
leaves dsh; in the rules file each one is a *rule*.
## Highlights
[该节后续省略]
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
If you run dsh from source, use `pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-request-params`. Restart `dsh
web` afterwards. A **Request Params** entry appears in the sidebar below **Plugins**.
[该节后续省略]
## What you can add
| Kind | Adds | Typical use |
| **Provider routing** | `provider` (`order`, `only`, `ignore`, `allow_fallbacks`, `require_paramete
rs`, `data_collection`, `zdr`, `quantizations`, `sort`, `max_price`, `preferred_min_throughput`, `pr
eferred_max_latency`, `enforce_distillable_text`) and `models` | Choose providers and order, cap the

price, require zero data retention, fall back to other models |
| **Reasoning effort** | `reasoning

` (`effort`, `max_tokens`, `exclude`) | Turn thinking up or down, or keep it out of the reply |
| **
Sampling extras** | `top_k`, `min_p`, `top_a`, `repetition_penalty` | Sampling fields the standard A

PI does not have |
| **Session stickiness** | `session_id` in the body and the `x-session-id` header

| Keep one conversation on one provider so caches hit |
| **App attribution** | `HTTP-Referer` and
`X-OpenRouter-Title` headers | Credit your traffic to your app on OpenRouter (dsh does not send thes

e) |
| **Remove fields** | removes fields such as `store` | A gateway that rejects a field dsh sends

|
| **Custom fields and headers** | anything: JSON fields, headers, removals | Any other gateway |
Which kinds a channel offers first follows what it reads (see **What a channel reads** below). An Op
enRouter channel offers every kind; a channel that reads the OpenAI format offers sampling extras, c
ustom fields, session stickiness, and remove fields; an Anthropic channel offers the last three. The
examples for other gateways (turn thinking off on a self-hosted vLLM with `chat_template_kwargs`, H
elicone headers, Cloudflare AI Gateway cache headers, and an OpenAI `prompt_cache_key`) come first o
n a channel that is that gateway. Everything else is under **Other kinds**, each marked with what it
needs, and can still be added. Each example is an ordinary custom parameter you can edit. **Other a
ddresses** offers everything.
## What a channel reads
Under its address, each channel shows its protocol: the request format it reads and the extra fields
, each channel shows its protocol: the request format it reads and the extra fields it reads on top.
[该节后续省略]
## Safety and privacy
- `messages`, `system`, `tools`, `tool_choice`, `input`, `instructions`, `prompt`, `contents`, `stre

am`, and `model` cannot be set or removed unless a custom parameter explicitly allows it.
- `Authori
zation`, `x-api-key`, `api-key`, `x-goog-api-key`, `Cookie`, `Host`, and the headers that frame the

request (`Content-Length`, `Content-Type`, …) can never be changed.
- A parameter with a problem is
not applied, and the page shows what is wrong. If applying parameters fails while a request is being

sent, the request goes out unchanged and the log says so.
- Parameters are stored on your machine i

n `<profile>/.dsh-request-params/config.json`. Nothing is sent anywhere because of them.
- The reque
st log lives in memory only (the last 50 requests; cleared on restart). It holds the model, the addr
ess, and the changes made; for a failed request it also keeps the first 2 KB of the gateway's answer
, which can quote the request. It never holds the conversation itself. Values from environment varia

bles appear as "not shown", and are replaced with `[env]` if the gateway's answer quotes them.
- The
channel list comes from dsh's own channel list and settings (with secrets redacted), to show each c

hannel's address and models; the page changes nothing there and stores nothing.
- The page reaches t
he network for two things. OpenRouter's public catalog (`/providers`, `/models`, `/models/{id}/endpo
ints`) is read only while the page shows a provider routing parameter: the provider list, the provid
ers that serve the previewed model, and fallback model suggestions; the provider list also works off
line from a built-in copy. The update check asks the npm registry DSH is configured with for this pl
ugin's latest version (see Updates). Neither sends a key or any content.
## How it works
[该节后续省略]
## Compatibility and limits

- Needs dsh with the web client and Node `^22.19.0 || >=24`. Tested with dsh 0.2.1-rc.2.
- Verified
against real dsh runs on three kinds of channel: the official DeepSeek endpoint (`/v1/messages`), an
OpenAI-compatible `llm-pi-ai` channel (`/chat/completions`), and an Anthropic-compatible `llm-pi-ai

` channel (`/v1/messages`).
- Applies to requests sent through the global `fetch`. A provider that c

aptured its own `fetch` earlier would not be seen; the request log shows what the plugin saw.
- A ga
teway may ignore or reject fields it does not know. OpenRouter ignores unsupported parameters unless

`require_parameters` is on.
- Limits: 100 parameters; per parameter, 64 KB of JSON each for the bod
y fields and the defaults, and 40 headers.
